articles.title: Sophie Cunningham could be on her way out of Indiana as the Fever face a major offseason decision
articles.standfirst: The shooting guard will be a free agent after a season in which she stood out off the bench. Stephanie White has already explained what type of players Indiana needs to take the next step.
articles.summary: The shooting guard will be a free agent after a season in which she stood out off the bench. Stephanie White has already explained what type of players Indiana needs to take the next step.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham’s future with the Indiana Fever is yet to be decided. After their elimination by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the WNBA playoffs, the franchise must begin planning for next season with Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston as its cornerstones. But there are two issues that require immediate attention: Cunningham and Kelsey Mitchell are both at the end of their contracts and will be unrestricted free agents.

Cunningham was Indiana's leading scorer off the bench in 2026, averaging 7.9 points per game and shooting 41.9% from three-point range in 43 games. Her production dipped during August and September, and she averaged 7.3 points in the series against Las Vegas. General manager Amber Cox valued her leadership and presence in the locker room, although she did not confirm whether the franchise will seek to re-sign her.

Stephanie White explained what Indiana needs

'Coach Stephanie White gave a hint about the direction she wants for the team. In addition to trying to retain Mitchell, she pointed out that the Fever need to find "complementary pieces for our Big 3", made up of Mitchell, Clark, and Boston.'

White described the profile she is looking for: a long, athletic forward, capable of defending the perimeter, pressuring opponents, helping on the boards, attacking the rim, and providing a constant threat from three-point range. She also highlighted the importance of getting more consistent production from the bench.

Cunningham has one of the virtues that fit that idea: outside shooting. In her two seasons with Indiana, she made 42.4% of her three-pointers. However, defense could be a decisive factor in determining her place in the project. The player herself acknowledged that she wants to raise her intensity in that area and establish herself as a 3-and-D specialist, that is, a player who contributes both on defense and in three-point shooting.

About her future, Cunningham avoided making predictions. "I don’t know what the offseason has in store for me", she said on her podcast No Hesitation.

Caitlin Clark also referred to the team’s makeup and pointed to defense as one of the areas Indiana must improve in order to compete more consistently. Her approach aligns with White’s pursuit: a team capable of maintaining its offensive production and responding better on the other side of the court.

Kelsey Mitchell, the Fever's priority

Kelsey Mitchell's situation could affect the rest of the moves. The shooting guard is coming off averaging 24.7 points per game, and the franchise has expressed its desire to keep her long term . However, Mitchell also did not guarantee her continuity and acknowledged that she will have to weigh her own interests before making a decision.

The player also spoke about the emotional toll that constant exposure surrounding the team and having to compete under the scrutiny of the fans can create. Her statements added another dimension to a negotiation that is not limited to the sporting aspect.

Clark, for her part, expressed her desire to keep playing alongside Mitchell and backed her teammate after her comments about the pressure surrounding the Fever. For Indiana, retaining one of its leading scorers appears to be one of the market’s priorities. What happens with Mitchell will also influence planning for the rest of the roster.

When will Sophie Cunningham's future be known?

The exact date of WNBA free agency for 2027 has not yet been officially confirmed. Therefore, there is no specific day to know whether Cunningham will stay in Indiana or listen to offers from other franchises. The negotiation will also depend on how the new Fever roster is resolved and how much room remains to strengthen other positions.

While awaiting that decision, Cunningham already has work scheduled. The American will play in Project B, a new international professional 5-on-5 league set to begin in 2027 and travel through cities in Europe, Asia, and America. The project was co-founded by Grady Burnett, a former Facebook and Google executive, and Geoff Prentice, co-founder of Skype, and will also feature Kelsey Mitchell. Cunningham explained that she plans to play from January to April, just before WNBA training camp. Valencia, from March 12 to 22, and Tokyo, from March 26 to April 4, are already among the confirmed stops of a competition that aims to operate with a traveling Grand Prix format.

“It’s going to be incredible. I’m going to play from January to April, until training camp begins. We’re going to be in several countries,” Cunningham said on October 5. “It will be a great opportunity to expand my brand globally, but at the same time I’ll be able to come back, keep making money, and also enjoy the offseason.”

Cunningham's continuity remains open . Her ability to score from the perimeter and her experience in the locker room work in her favor, but Indiana is looking to improve its defense and first needs to resolve Mitchell's future. Those decisions will determine how much of a place the guard will have in the project the Fever are building around Clark and Boston.

articles.title: Who is favored to win the WNBA finals? Expert picks, predictions and odds for the Golden State Valkyries vs Atlanta Dream series
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are preparing to compete for their first WNBA championship, with the 2026 Finals beginning on October 17
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are preparing to compete for their first WNBA championship, with the 2026 Finals beginning on October 17
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Finals will feature an unexpected but compelling matchup between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream .

Both teams have eliminated established championship contenders to reach the final, setting up a best-of-seven series with a historic prize at stake.

According to the latest odds published by the WNBA through BetMGM, the Valkyries are slight favorites to win the championship, priced at -115, while Atlanta is listed at -105.

Those numbers indicate a narrow advantage for Golden State rather than a decisive prediction that the series will go its way.

The Finals begin Saturday, October 17, at Chase Center in San Francisco. Golden State earned home-court advantage after finishing the regular season with a 32-12 record, while Atlanta enters the championship round as the fourth seed after a 30-14 campaign.

Both teams have built momentum at exactly the right time, although their paths to the final have been different.

Golden State reached the Finals in only its second season as a WNBA franchise. The Valkyries followed a hard-fought first-round series against Dallas by sweeping the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals.

Atlanta, meanwhile, swept Washington before eliminating the New York Liberty in three games, leaving the Dream undefeated in the playoffs.

That contrast makes this matchup particularly intriguing. Golden State has the benefit of home court and a reputation for defensive discipline, while Atlanta has demonstrated that it can handle high-pressure games and produce offense against elite opposition.

Expert predictions: Why Golden State has the edge, but Atlanta cannot be dismissed

The betting market gives Golden State a narrow advantage, and several analysts have also backed the Valkyries to win the series. However, expert predictions are far from unanimous, with some believing Atlanta's offensive depth and recent improvement could be decisive.

In predictions published by The Athletic and republished by Yahoo Sports, Brian Hamilton selected Golden State to win in six games, while Marcus Thompson II backed the Valkyries in seven.

Annie Costabile and Chantel Jennings both predicted an Atlanta victory in seven games, illustrating how closely matched the finalists appear.

Golden State's strongest argument is its defense. The Valkyries limited the Las Vegas Aces during their semifinal sweep and have relied on collective effort, depth and disciplined preparation throughout the postseason.

Gabby Williams has also emerged as a major offensive contributor, giving the team a player capable of making a difference when games become tight.

Atlanta has its own reasons for confidence. Angel Reese has been influential on the boards, while Jordin Canada has supplied scoring and playmaking. Rhyne Howard remains an important perimeter threat, and DeWanna Bonner 's experience gives the Dream another option in crucial moments.

The availability of Allisha Gray could be one of the most important variables. The Atlanta guard injured her left hand during the semifinals and underwent a minor procedure, leaving her status for the start of the Finals uncertain.

If she is unable to play or is limited, the Dream could lose a key part of their scoring attack.

articles.title: Tennis legend Chris Evert calls for a tribute to Caitlin Clark following her controversial remarks
articles.standfirst: Former World No. 1 tennis star believes the WNBA should embrace Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Former World No. 1 tennis star believes the WNBA should embrace Caitlin Clark
articles.body:
Tennis legend Chris Evert has renewed her support for Caitlin Clark , arguing that the WNBA should celebrate the Indiana Fever star and the attention she’s brought to women’s basketball.

“The WNBA should be celebrating her,” Evert wrote on X, replying to a viral post describing Clark as the most powerful female athlete in the world. The wording wasn’t quite accurate.

In October 2025, Forbes published “America’s Most Powerful Women in Sports.” Clark ranked fourth, behind New Orleans Saints and Pelicans owner Gayle Benson , FanDuel chief executive Amy Howe and Nike executive Amy Montagne.

She was the highest-ranked active athlete on that list, but it covered influential American women in sports rather than naming the world’s most powerful female athlete.

Other sports figures recognized included Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart , who were listed together at ninth, tennis great Serena Williams at 11, Coco Gauff at 13 and four-time WNBA MVP A’ja Wilson at 15. Even with the viral claim needing clarification, Clark’s place on the list reflected her growing profile beyond basketball.

Clark’s arrival in the league in 2024 coincided with a substantial increase in attention. The WNBA drew more than 54 million unique viewers across national television networks during her rookie season, while total attendance rose 48% from the previous year.

The Fever also recorded 340,715 fans at home games, surpassing the New York Liberty’s previous league benchmark of 250,565, set in 2001. Clark wasn’t solely responsible for the league’s growth, but her popularity was an important factor.

Clark’s influence reaches far beyond the court

That audience interest has continued. In 2026, Fever games featuring Clark were among the most-watched WNBA broadcasts on CBS, ESPN and ION. An Indiana matchup against the Chicago Sky also became the second-most-watched WNBA game in ABC history, underscoring the star’s continuing drawing power.

The impact is visible on social media, too. Research by Indiana University Columbus finance professor Ryan Brewer found that official WNBA social-media views climbed from 373 million in late 2023 to nearly 2 billion by the end of the 2024 season, a 436% year-over-year increase.

Brewer compared the excitement around Clark to the “Taylor Swift effect,” while stressing that other players contribute to the league’s appeal. Clark’s highlights, he found, can attract far more views than typical WNBA game content.

Evert’s latest comment is consistent with her previous public support. When Clark was named TIME’s 2024 Athlete of the Year, Evert said she deserved the honor after Washington Mystics co-owner Sheila Johnson questioned the decision.

In June 2025, Evert also criticized poor sportsmanship after Clark was poked in the eye during a game against the Connecticut Sun.

Evert’s message is familiar, as she believes Clark’s popularity should be viewed as an opportunity. Recognizing one star doesn’t mean overlooking her teammates.

articles.title: Lexie Hull's emotional goodbye fuels uncertainty over Sophie Cunningham's Indiana Fever future
articles.standfirst: The player closed out her fifth season with the Fever with a message that sparked a flood of responses from Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston, and several of her teammates, although her future in Indiana is not in doubt.
articles.summary: The player closed out her fifth season with the Fever with a message that sparked a flood of responses from Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston, and several of her teammates, although her future in Indiana is not in doubt.
articles.body:
"L The season ended days ago for the Indiana Fever, but some of its leading figures are still processing a finish that came earlier than expected. Lexie Hull was one of them and used her social media to sum up what it meant to complete her fifth year with the franchise.

"Half a decade with Indiana Fever," Hull wrote alongside a carousel of photos from the season. The message was a reflection on her five years with the organization, but the tone of some of the replies made the post seem, at times, like a farewell.

Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and the Fever react to Lexie Hull

Hull's teammates were quick to appear in the comments. Myisha Hines-Allen wrote "I already miss you", while Caitlin Clark replied with five pink hearts. Tyasha Harris left an "Lexxxxxx" accompanied by a heart.

Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston also took part. Mitchell used her teammate's nickname, "sexy lexi", while Boston wrote "I'm proud of you, sexyyyy lexiiii" Grace VanSlooten, Raven Johnson, and Monique Billings also joined in with messages.

The reaction makes sense because of the bond Hull has built with Indiana. The franchise selected her with the No. 6 pick in the 2022 Draft and since then she has played her entire WNBA career with the Fever.

In 2026, Hull started 41 games and averaged 5.2 points and 3.0 rebounds in 18.2 minutes per game.

The message doesn't mean Lexie Hull is leaving Indiana

Although the tone of the post may sound like a farewell, Hull is not saying goodbye to the Fever . Indiana agreed to a two-season contract extension with her worth around $1.6 million, so she is under contract through 2027.

What did come to an end was a season that left mixed feelings in Indianapolis. Indiana finished the regular season with a 28-16 record and placed sixth in the standings. In the playoffs, the Fever took their first-round series against the Las Vegas Aces to a third game, but were ultimately eliminated after losing 94-83.

Hull, therefore, has her continuity assured. The uncertainty lies in other pieces of the roster.

Sophie Cunningham, one of the pending decisions

The situation is especially interesting in the case of Sophie Cunningham, who faces an open future after her first full season with Indiana. Her continuity will be one of the decisions the franchise will have to address during the offseason.

Kelsey Mitchell's future, one of the team's main offensive references, also remains to be resolved as she enters free agency. Caitlin Clark herself publicly expressed her desire for Mitchell to remain in Indiana.

With Hull under contract through 2027, Clark and Aliyah Boston as central pieces, and several decisions still pending, Indiana faces an offseason with changes yet to be defined.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s “Taylor Swift effect” sent WNBA social views from 373 million to nearly 2 billion
articles.standfirst: A study found that views on the league’s official social media accounts more than quintupled after Clark’s rookie season
articles.summary: A study found that views on the league’s official social media accounts more than quintupled after Clark’s rookie season
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s impact is showing up somewhere beyond the box score: on fans’ screens. Views across the WNBA’s official social media accounts rose from 373 million in late 2023 to 1.96 billion after the 2024 season, according to a study by Indiana University Columbus finance professor Ryan Brewer. That’s more than five times the earlier total.

Brewer described the attention around Clark as a “Taylor Swift effect.” His comparison points to the kind of fascination that can draw people in beyond the usual audience. “People are fascinated by Clark,” he told The Indianapolis Star . The numbers don’t mean Clark alone accounts for the league’s growth: the study covers a season shaped by a celebrated rookie class, including Angel Reese, and the WNBA’s official accounts overall.

Clark’s highlights can turn a play into a viral moment

The scale is especially striking around Clark’s biggest plays. Brewer told the Star that highlights featuring Clark drew between 20 million and 45 million views across TikTok, X and Instagram, compared with roughly 3 million to 5 million for a WNBA game without her.

He said Clark generates 800% more viral views when her plays and highlights are featured. Those are view counts, not a tally of unique people.

The attention has carried into 2026. Brewer’s research found that Clark and the Fever generated more social media views than the rest of the league combined.

On television, Indiana’s Game 3 matchup with the Las Vegas Aces averaged 2.25 million viewers on USA Network and CNBC, making it the second most-watched first-round playoff game on record and the most-watched WNBA playoff game since 2024.

That is the larger story behind the “Taylor Swift effect”: one star can become an entry point to a whole league. Brewer stressed that basketball remains a team sport, and said fans are also noticing the other players around Clark.

The view counts show just how bright the spotlight has become. The league’s next challenge is to turn that attention into lasting interest that extends well beyond any one player by making the WNBA more competitive and, above all, fair and transparent.
